As part of the restructuring, we intend to discontinue the origination of retail and wholesale SBL loans by the end of 2026 while continuing to manage the existing SBL loan portfolio.

As part of our long-term strategic plan, in September 2026, we announced that as part of our organizational restructuring, we intend to discontinue the origination of retail and wholesale SBL loans by the end of 2026.

We expect to continue to increase the proportion of Fintech loans in our portfolio through the remainder of 2026 and beyond, and therefore we expect to see continued compression in our average rate earned on loans, and net interest margin, as the mix of fintech loans continues to grow.
However, we also expect growth in our fintech fees within non-interest income driven by the increase in that portfolio.

We expect to continue to invest in tax credits in future periods, resulting in an estimated annual future effective tax rate of approximately 23.9%, compared to the full year 2025 effective tax rate of 24.7%.

We expect to continue to increase the proportion of Fintech loans in our portfolio for the remainder of 2026 and beyond, and therefore we expect to see continued compression in our average rate earned on loans, and net interest margin, as the mix of fintech loans continues to grow.

We review the adequacy of our ACL on at least a quarterly basis to determine a provision for credit losses to maintain our ACL at a level we believe is appropriate to recognize current expected credit losses.
The measurement of the estimated credit losses and the expected recovery from the credit enhancement are based on the same estimate and correlate to like amounts in our financial statements.
We expect to continue to maintain our facilities with the FHLB and Federal Reserve.
